en.title: First Time a Fully Black Square Appears
en.description:
On a white n×m canvas, one given cell is painted black every minute, and each cell appears exactly once. Find the minute at which a fully painted k×k square first exists.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m k, followed by n×m lines of 1-indexed coordinates, all distinct. 1≤n,m≤750; 1≤k≤min(n,m).
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers to the three examples are 1, 4 and 4; in the third example the left square is completed first.
hints: Fill each cell with the minute it is painted; a square is complete at the maximum time inside it. Use a monotonic queue first along rows and then along columns to get the 2D k-window maximum, then take the minimum.
